title: The present band: bass and guitar
summary: Johnston asks for names and instruments. Gil discusses bassist Herb Bushler and the Fender bass, then guitarist Ted Dunbar.

story.theme_name: Drummers and drumming: who played what, and how
story.community_name: Bass players: lineage, tone and technique

blocks.x: Would you at this point name the players and instruments in your band, your present band? And separate them into those who play the accoustical instruments and those who play the electronic ones. Is that too difficult? (LAUGHTER).
I know that we can almost forget the names of our sisters and brothers. (LAUGHTER).
thought you meant Well I name the instruments like the trumpet, the trombone.....
Well I did mean the instruments, but if you could put the names of your present players together with them I think that would be helpful.

Well, it hasn't been determined, I haven't got the answer for this since I don't have steady work, I don't have a steady band. But I do have the names that I call the same players to see if they can play, you know.
Give us the names of the instruments then.

I have the bass, (Herb Bushler) can play the bass with me on Monday night. He plays acoustic bass and (Fender) electric bass. Although the acoustic bass is also amplified. And if you turn it up too loud it does really sound as, it doesn't sound as good as the (Fender) does. You had better use the (Fender) if you are going to use it for certain things.
Why is the (Fender ?) bass called Fender bass?
It's just a company name. It used to be called an electric bass.
The name of the company is Fender and that's the most popular ............ ............ ............ ............(VOICE FADES OUT).
I think this has been a very great thing, you know, ............ ............

Actually the (Fender?) bass is not really a, it's an electric, it's an electric creation, you know. That's what it is. It has a characteristic sound. And based on certain jazz Brown bass players somewhat like Ray and Paul Chambers I feel that whoever set that bass sound had to have them in mind. one.

And then I have a guitarist Ted Dunbar. He plays electric guitar. Oh he plays acoustic guitar too, but mostly electric and he teaches at Rutgers. I think. They have another school connected with Rutgers, is it Livingston? There is a jazz course there and he teaches there and gets $11,000.
He wanted to know if I wanted the job. It isn't a hard job. He only owes them nine hours a week, and he gets $11,000. And he says he doesn't, he only uses three hours and a half.

And I'm trying to have two guitars. And I'm very fortunate in getting them together to rehearse and develop the two guitars. And then I have a synthesizer. We don't have a synthesizer right now except the one, he has a little Putney which is hard to do a good job because it's hard to change. It needs to be retuned, but it's not a new person on the job for a synthesizer.
